item.SHORT_TEXT: ORTEC: serialize a bounded batch of objects (aRFC worker)
item.DOCUMENTATION:
Multi-object batch serialization worker for the ORTEC adaptive serialization orchestrator (ZCL_ABAPGIT_ORTEC_SER_ORCH).
INTENDED USE: called ONLY by ZCL_ABAPGIT_ORTEC_SER_ORCH via "CALL FUNCTION 'Z_ABAPGIT_ORTEC_SER_BATCH' STARTING NEW TASK ...". Not intended for direct use by any other caller.
PARAMETERS: IV_BATCH_ID - logical grouping id for this dispatch, stable across a batch's own retries/bisections (telemetry/correlation only - the caller's callback resolves results by RFC task name, never by this id). IV_ATTEMPT - 1 for a group's first dispatch, incremented by the caller for each retry/bisection of the same logical group; carried through purely for telemetry/log correlation, has no effect on this worker's own logic. IV_ABAP_LANGUAGE_VERS - ABAP language version to serialize objects under, same meaning and type as the existing single-object Z_ABAPGIT_SERIALIZE_PARALLEL's own IV_ABAP_LANGUAGE_VERS parameter. IV_LANGUAGE - main serialization language (SY-LANGU), applied to every object in this batch. IV_PATH - target repository path, passed through unchanged to each object's own serialize() call, exactly like the existing single-object worker's IV_PATH. IV_MAIN_LANGUAGE_ONLY - X = skip translation-language texts for every object in this batch (matches the existing single-object worker's flag of the same name). IV_SUPPRESS_PO_COMMENTS - X = suppress PO-file comments for every object in this batch (matches the existing single-object worker's flag). IV_USE_LXE - X = use the LXE translation environment instead of the classic per-language text serialization path, for every object in this batch (matches the existing single-object worker's flag). IT_TRANSLATION_LANGS - languages to serialize translation texts for, when IV_MAIN_LANGUAGE_ONLY is not set; same meaning as the existing single- object worker's parameter of the same name. IT_TADIR - the bounded set of objects to serialize in this ONE dispatch (never the whole repository - the caller/planner is responsible for row/byte budgeting before dispatch). Every row produces exactly one ET_RESULT row. IV_PREFETCH_BUFFER / IV_PREFETCH_BUFFER_EXT / IV_PREFETCH_BUFFER_OO - optional EXPORT-to-buffer prefetch data for the existing ZCL_ABAPGIT_ORTEC_SER_PREF/_EXT/_OO caches, injected into THIS worker session before any object is serialized (mirrors the existing single- object worker's own injection pattern) - initial/omitted means that provider family has nothing prefetched for this batch (normal per- object serialization is used instead, never an error). IV_PREFETCH_BUFFER_DD - reserved for the SER-SLICE-3 DOMA/DTEL provider; always initial/unused in SER-SLICE-2 - no SER-SLICE-3 provider logic is implemented by this function module yet. IV_INPUT_ROW_COUNT - number of rows the caller intended to send in IT_TADIR, for a cross-check that the worker received exactly the batch the caller dispatched. IV_INPUT_VERSION - version of the caller/worker contract this call was built against; must match between caller and worker code generations (see INPUT/RESULT VERSION COMPATIBILITY below). ET_RESULT - one row per IT_TADIR object, success or failure, in the same order objects were processed; see ZAOG_SER_BATCH_RESULT field-level documentation for the exact result shape. EV_OUTPUT_ROW_COUNT - number of rows actually returned in ET_RESULT, letting the caller cross-check it received a result for the complete batch it dispatched (always equal to the number of rows in IT_TADIR when ERROR was not raised).
One call processes a BOUNDED batch of objects (IT_TADIR), never the whole repository - the caller (the planner) is responsible for row/byte budgeting before dispatch. Every object in IT_TADIR produces exactly one ET_RESULT row (success or failure) - a single object's failure never discards or hides another object's successful result in the same batch.
WORKER-SESSION LIFECYCLE: this function module may serialize MULTIPLE DIFFERENT objects, one after another, inside the SAME RFC work-process session (unlike the existing single-object Z_ABAPGIT_SERIALIZE_PARALLEL, which always processes exactly one). The OD-14 static-state audit (.memory/logs/serialization_slice_2_od14_audit.md) confirms no unmitigated unsafe cross-object state for the object types this worker is used for.
INPUT/RESULT VERSION COMPATIBILITY: IV_INPUT_VERSION and the ET_RESULT row shape are versioned together - a caller and worker built from different code generations must not be mixed; IV_INPUT_ROW_COUNT lets the worker cross-check it received exactly the batch the caller intended to send.
No WAPA object is ever processed by this function module in SER-SLICE-2 - WAPA remains on its existing, unchanged, single-object serialization path.
TRANSACTION: no explicit COMMIT WORK/ROLLBACK WORK is issued here beyond whatever the underlying per-object serialize() call already does today; see serialization_performance_design.md §3a for the accepted implicit- commit-cadence analysis.
FAILURE HANDLING: system/communication/resource failures (the whole RFC call not completing) are NOT represented inside ET_RESULT - they surface to the caller as a failed RECEIVE, and are handled entirely by the orchestrator's own retry/bisection/fallback logic, never inside this function module. The ERROR exception here is reserved for a batch-level failure that prevents this worker from even attempting any object in the batch (for example, prefetch-buffer injection itself failing) - it is never raised for an individual object's own serialization failure, which is always represented as a normal (non-exceptional) ET_RESULT row with RC <> 0 instead.
No scheduling/cost statistics are persisted anywhere by this function module - ET_RESULT's ELAPSED_MS/OUTPUT_BYTES fields are read back by the orchestrator's run-local (in-memory only) adaptive cost estimator and never written to any database table.
